observations: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
A1: Preview banner: “Evaluation preview · learning history and analytics are not saved.”
A2: Prediction: Greenland drawn about15times Congo on map; “On the real Earth, how do their areas compare?”; choices Greenland15×/Greenland1×/Congo4×; selected Greenland15× and locked.
A3: Mercator at73°N:15.4×; set Slide south40:33°N and1.4×; screenshot shows small blue translated Greenland and dashed original outline.
A4: Clicked Slide to equator:73°south,0.9×; clicked Equal-area map: equal-area0.9×, orange compass-bearing line bent instead of straight; Show me why enabled.
A5: Returned slider0 on equal-area map:73°N still0.9×; Seen line retained “Mercator15.4× at73°N,0.9×at the equator; equal-area0.9×”.

A6: Reveal: “Not quite: it was ‘Greenland about1×Congo’.”; Congo slightly bigger2.17vs2.34million km²; “The land never changed; the map did.”; Mercator stretches areas farther from equator and keeps angles true; orange compass-bearing line straight there and bent on equal-area; “No flat map can keep both.”

prediction.reason: The question separates apparent map area from real land area with plausible alternatives and explicit commitment.

interaction.reason: Latitude changes and projection switching expose both Mercator's changing scale and equal-area invariance across controlled contrasts.

payoff.reason: The reveal resolves the original prediction using the retained observed ratios and explains the area-versus-angle trade-off shown by the orange line.

clarity.reason: The stepwise instruction and retained Seen line make the tested two-control sequence interpretable.

transfer.reason: The projection trade-off provides a relevant condition for comparing land areas versus maintaining compass directions.

accessibility.reason: No keyboard, phone, contrast, zoom/reflow or reduced-motion checks were performed.
evidence: Desktop AX snapshots and screenshots only; accessible labels observed but insufficient for an accessibility rating.

surprise.reason: The committed15× guess reverses through intermediate1.4×, equator0.9× and equal-area invariance.

visualExplanation.reason: The visibly shrinking translated shape and straight-versus-bent line carry multiple projection contrasts.

playfulness.reason: The reversible latitude slider and projection toggle make experimentation central.

practicalValue.reason: The reveal supports better map interpretation with concrete area and navigation conditions.

depth.reason: Distinct latitude scaling, equal-area invariance and compass-line geometry remain observable across multiple states.

complexity.reason: Against the declared boundary, learners coordinate geographic position, area ratios and two projections, with retained observations supporting the transition.
complexity.boundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no map-projection, sorting-algorithm or sound-propagation theory assumed.

whyCool: Sliding Greenland south shrinks its drawn ratio from15.4× to0.9× while the equal-area map keeps0.9× even back at73°N.
caveat: The angle-versus-area explanation adds an unfamiliar compass-bearing concept without a separate learner application check.
